newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Man jailed for threatening Sweden's richest man.
newsitem.headline: Man jailed for threatening Sweden's richest man.

text.p: A 25-year-old Swedish man was jailed for two years on Wednesday for threatening Sweden's richest man, Stefan Persson, who runs the successful high-street fashion chain Hennes & Mauritz (H&M).
Stockholm's local court heard the man delivered a threatening letter to H&M's head office in central Stockholm in early May this year.
The letter pledged bomb threats against Persson and his family every Friday until Persson handed over 10 million crowns ($1.3 million), Swedish news agency TT reported.
Persson alerted the police and his security staff and the man was arrested after delivering the letter.
But the man told the court that he was just the messenger and knew nothing about the contents of the letter. He said he only expected to receive 5,000 crowns for delivering it.
But the court dismissed the man's plea of innocence and sentenced him to two years imprisonment.
Persson was listed as the richest man residing in Sweden earlier this year with his family owning shares worth over 17 billion crowns on the Stockholm stock market.
